executableSurface.repositoryResolution: git rev-parse --show-toplevel from the current directory, then full-path normalised and compared to the lab root by exact equality or a StartsWith on labRoot + path separator, which is what blocks a sibling directory sharing the name prefix

executableSurface.failureHandling: every git call goes through Invoke-GitChecked, which treats the child exit code as authoritative rather than the presence of stderr and throws with rendered output on nonzero; the script sets ErrorActionPreference Stop, so a throw exits nonzero
executableSurface.dirtyTree: warns only; pushes committed HEAD and modifies no local file

refusalBeforeMutation.how: every case declares its exact permitted push count; precondition refusals declare zero, the accepted branch declares one, and the post-attempt failures declare exactly one attempted push followed by the failure

observations.detail: Previously a branch differing only in letter case was accepted and pushed. The hardened harness demonstrated it, and the -cnotcontains edit closed it. Two cases now pin the refusal.

If git emitted no line at all for branch --show-current the wrapper would fail on a null method call instead of its detached-HEAD message. Real git prints an empty line, which reaches the intended refusal. It refuses either way.

reviewedNewBaseline.conclusion: The current script is adopted as the reviewed new baseline. This accepts the loss of exact prior byte reconstruction and certifies present behaviour only; it does not certify historical equivalence and does not relax any push rule.
futureEditProtocol: prove that removing the inserted byte span reproduces the pre-edit hash

caseSensitiveBranchHardening.authority: owner order of 2026-10-16 section 2B, a narrow containment hardening
caseSensitiveBranchHardening.why: Git refs differing only in case can be distinct refs, so a differently cased spelling is not the authorized ref. The previous comparison used PowerShell -notcontains, which is case-insensitive, and the hardened harness demonstrated the wrapper accepting and pushing a case variant before the change.
caseSensitiveBranchHardening.change: one comparison operator: -notcontains became -cnotcontains on the branch check
caseSensitiveBranchHardening.scope: branch membership only. The origin, qualified-baseline ancestry, repository-root and destructive-operation restrictions are untouched, and the Windows path comparisons remain case-insensitive because file paths are not Git refs.

escalatedDecision.decisionText: Brachiosaurus gets three roots on Summon Nature's Ally only - VII one, VIII 1d3, IX 1d4+1 - with no Summon Monster row and no celestial/fiendish execution children.
escalatedDecision.decisionRationaleRecorded: The order was followed as written. Because identities are allocated once and append-only, this is the reversible direction: adding the Summon Monster VII rows in a later sprint is purely additive, whereas publishing Monster rows the owner did not want could not be cleanly withdrawn. The source discrepancy is preserved in this ledger rather than discarded, so a later sprint can act on it without re-deriving it.

donorRig.classificationCorrection: The earlier record classified this rig from BONE NAMES and was wrong in the way that mattered most. It reported a single twelve-joint tail chain and no trunk chain, and concluded that a long sauropod neck on this donor could only be a rigid two-segment structure. Re-reading the captured world positions and the parent chain shows that conclusion does not hold.
donorRig.spatialMethod: The body axis is taken from LowerTorso to UpperTorso, which is unambiguous and points toward the front of the animal. Every joint is then placed by its signed distance along that axis from LowerTorso. Nothing in this record depends on a bone name.

forwardChain.whatItActuallyIs: The TRUNK. It is parented to Head and extends forward of it, and the engine hangs its own Locator_Head_02, _03, _04, _05 and _06 off these joints rather than off Head. A chain named Tail that is parented to the head and runs forward from it is not a tail.

rearChain.whatItActuallyIs: The real tail. Parented to LowerTorso and running behind it.

donorRig.whatThisChangesForBrachiosaurus: The rig does carry an articulated forward chain: seven skinned joints running forward from the head, as long as the whole UpperTorso-to-Head span. That is the natural carrier for a long sauropod neck, so the "rigid pole neck" finding is withdrawn. The approach it implies is a bounded retarget rather than new bones: author the neck along the forward chain with the creature head at the chain tip, leaving the native Head joint at the neck base. The existing five-joint rear chain stays with the real tail, which the 4d6 tail attack needs, so nothing is borrowed away from the attack.
donorRig.whatThisChangesForElephant: The released Elephant has a seven-joint articulated trunk after all. The earlier claim that there is no trunk chain is withdrawn.
donorRig.stillToProve: Spatial classification establishes what the chains ARE. It does not establish that the native animation drives them the way an authored neck needs, which is what the graybox motion prototype is for: idle, walk, turn, attack and trample, plus interruption and death transitions, before any final geometry or texture work.
donorRig.notAnAcceptedLimitation: No visual limitation is proposed and no waiver is requested. The four inherited limitations are unchanged.

trampleArithmeticRepair.kind: source-contract inconsistency, not a reproduced native damage defect
trampleArithmeticRepair.theTwoFormulas: GiantBodyRulesPolicy.TrampleStrengthContribution delegated to the lone-natural-weapon helper, which multiplies only a positive modifier and leaves zero and penalties at face value. UngulateRulesProfile.TrampleBonusFor multiplied unconditionally as liveStrengthModifier * 3 / 2 whenever LiveTrampleMath is set, and both Sprint 25 creatures select that mode. At a live modifier of -4 the first gives -4 and the second gives -6; they also disagree at -2, -3 and -5. They agree at every printed positive baseline, which is why it survived.
trampleArithmeticRepair.whichOneActuallyRan: TrampleBonusFor. The damage path is ContextActionUngulateTrample line 122, damage.AddBonus(rules.TrampleBonusFor(liveStrengthModifier)). TrampleStrengthContribution is referenced only inside GiantBodyRulesPolicy.Validate at its two positive baselines and never reaches damage, so the record helper was the correct one and the runtime formula was the defect - the opposite of the convenient fix.
trampleArithmeticRepair.selectedRule: One and a half times a Strength BONUS. A penalty is not a bonus, so zero and negatives stay at face value. This is what the frozen contract already stated in two places, and what the printed trample rule says.
trampleArithmeticRepair.implementation: One authoritative implementation, UngulateRulesPolicy.OneAndAHalfStrength, on the shared carrier the damage path already reads. TrampleBonusFor and GoreBonus call it, and GiantBodyRulesPolicy.TrampleStrengthContribution delegates to it, so the record helper and the runtime are now literally the same code and cannot drift apart again.
trampleArithmeticRepair.changedDependency: Triceratops is the one released creature that shares the live branch, so it shares this repair. Its printed positive values are unchanged - 8 gives 12 and 10 gives 15, the existing Sprint 23 assertions - and only the penalty case moves, to the rule the record always stated. The five frozen-math tramplers never take the live branch and are untouched; the test asserts they ignore a live modifier entirely.
trampleArithmeticRepair.controlsRun: Focused run of 29 related tests, 0 failures: the new signed-Strength table plus the existing sprint11-trample-targets, sprint11-published-trample-contract, sprint23-trample-live-math and sprint15-stag-beetle-trample controls.
trampleArithmeticRepair.tableCovered: modifiers 13, 10, 8, 7, 5, 1, 0, -1, -2, -3, -4 and -5 through the same UngulateRulesProfile the damage path consumes, each cross-checked against the record helper, plus live DC cases for both creatures at positive and negative live Strength.
trampleArithmeticRepair.notAuthorityFor: a broad arithmetic refactor or a whole-roster replay. GoreBonus reads frozen positive Strengths, so no released attack value moves.

GreatCleave.identity: cc9c862ef2e03af4f89be5088851ea35 GreatCleaveFeature, BlueprintFeature, present in the installed library
GreatCleave.components: Two, both selection-time prerequisites: PrerequisiteFeature(CleaveFeature d809b6c4ff2aaff4fa70d712a70f7d7b) and PrerequisiteStatValue(Strength 13). No AddFacts and no granted ability.
GreatCleave.consumerSearchResult: FOUND, and the census caution was right to insist on this check. Native code does query a Great Cleave fact directly: Kingmaker.UnitLogic.Abilities.Components.AbilityCustomCleave declares "public BlueprintFeature GreaterFeature" and its Deliver coroutine reads caster.Descriptor.Progression.Features.HasFact(GreaterFeature) into a local isGreater. So a feature with no AddFacts is NOT automatically inert, and that assumption was correctly refused.
GreatCleave.provenBehaviouralDifference: From the IL of AbilityCustomCleave.<Deliver>d__3: for each candidate it triggers RuleAttackWithWeapon with IsFirstAttack set only for the first target; a miss (AttackRoll.IsHit false) breaks the chain in both cases; on a hit it yields the target and increments targetsHit; then "if (!isGreater && targetsHit > 1) break". Ordinary Cleave therefore stops after one extra target, and the greater path lifts the cap entirely. Great Cleave changes the target cap only - it is not an action-cost change, and the action cost lives on the CleaveAction blueprint.
GreatCleave.accessibilityOnThisBuild: THE DECISIVE FACT, and it is not what the printed rules imply. On the shipped CleaveAction (6447d104a2222c14d9c9b8a36e4eb242) the AbilityCustomCleave.GreaterFeature field points at CleaveFeature (d809b6c4ff2aaff4fa70d712a70f7d7b), NOT at GreatCleaveFeature. CleaveFeature is also what grants CleaveAction in the first place, via AddFacts. So HasFact(GreaterFeature) is true for anyone who can cleave at all, and isGreater is always set.
GreatCleave.consequenceForThisCreature: Two consequences. First, GreatCleaveFeature is read by nothing on this build: it has no components and the only native consumer does not point at it, so granting it to Brachiosaurus would change no behaviour. Second, the printed Great Cleave BEHAVIOUR - an uncapped cleave chain that continues while attacks hit - is already what the creature gets from the Cleave it already carries.
GreatCleave.disposition: RESOLVED. Not carried, and not needed: granting it would be exactly the inert display-only fact this order forbids labelling as implemented. The printed mechanical benefit is nevertheless present through the engine’s own wiring. No gameplay deviation and no waiver is requested. Note for the record that ordinary Cleave is more generous than printed on this build for every creature that has it, which is a pre-existing engine condition and not something this sprint introduces.
evidence: IL of Kingmaker.UnitLogic.Abilities.Components.AbilityCustomCleave, read from the private reference assembly; no game launch

GreaterOverrun.identity: ee24c02cc68c4c9b9b54ebef9f9f8133 GreaterOverrunFeature, BlueprintFeature, present in the installed library
GreaterOverrun.components: Two mechanical and four selection-time prerequisites. Mechanical: ManeuverProvokeAttack(Overrun) and ManeuverBonus(Overrun, +2). Prerequisites: Strength 13, BaseAttackBonus 6, PrerequisiteFeature(PowerAttackFeature) and PrerequisiteFeature(ImprovedOverrunFeature).
GreaterOverrun.whoProvokesFromWhomOnWhichEvent: Read from the IL of ManeuverProvokeAttack, not inferred from its name. The type extends RuleInitiatorLogicComponent<RuleCombatManeuver> and subscribes as IInitiatorRulebookHandler, so it is the initiator’s feat that owns it. OnEventAboutToTrigger is empty (a bare ret). OnEventDidTrigger is: if (evt.Type == this.ManeuverType) and evt.Success, then Game.Instance.CombatEngagementController.ProvokeAttackOfOpportunity(evt.Target). So the party that provokes is the maneuver’s TARGET, not the initiator; it happens after the maneuver resolves, and only on success. That matches the printed Greater Overrun rider exactly. It does not touch the rule’s IsGreater flag.
GreaterOverrun.maneuverBonusConsumer: ManeuverBonus extends RuleInitiatorLogicComponent<RuleCalculateCMB>, so the +2 applies only while a CMB is being calculated for the initiator.
GreaterOverrun.trampleConsumerClaimWithdrawn: WITHDRAWN as false. This ledger previously inferred a real consumer because ConfigureUngulateTrample clones native OverrunAbility 1a3b471ecea51f7439a946b23577fd70. Clone ancestry did not establish the configured graph’s behaviour, exactly as warned. The IL of AbilityCustomOverrun.<Deliver>d__9 branches on AutoSuccess BEFORE it constructs anything: if AutoSuccess is true it jumps past the "new RuleCombatManeuver(caster, target, Overrun)" and its context.TriggerRule call entirely. ExpandedSummoningSpecialBuilder sets overrun.AutoSuccess = true for every shipped trample. So a trample raises neither RuleCombatManeuver nor RuleCalculateCMB, and NEITHER Greater Overrun component can fire through trample.
GreaterOverrun.andThatIsFaithful: Printed trample requires no combat maneuver check, so the AutoSuccess trample is correct. Nothing was added to trample to manufacture a consumer: no maneuver check, no +2 to trample damage or DC, no change to its response options, and no forced knockdown or provocation.
GreaterOverrun.prerequisiteFinding: Answered separately, as required. PrerequisiteFeature and PrerequisiteStatValue derive from Prerequisite : BlueprintComponent and declare ZERO rulebook handlers, so they act only during feat selection in the level-up system. A direct blueprint grant bypasses them, and they have no effect during use. The missing Improved Overrun therefore would not block a direct grant of Greater Overrun, and no extra feat and no stat-block rewrite is needed to avoid the discrepancy.
GreaterOverrun.remainingOpenBehaviour: Whether this creature can reach an ORDINARY overrun maneuver at all. The components are real and would fire on a RuleCombatManeuver of type Overrun, which only an overrun ability with AutoSuccess false raises. What grants such an ability to a summon, and whether any supported command or AI path reaches it, is not established by the evidence gathered so far.
GreaterOverrun.exactFailedPath: Brachiosaurus carries no overrun ability. Its trample is AutoSuccess = true, which skips RuleCombatManeuver construction, so ManeuverBonus(Overrun, +2) and ManeuverProvokeAttack(Overrun) are both unreachable for it today.
GreaterOverrun.smallestGameplayChoice: Either (a) grant the native GreaterOverrunFeature as a faithful but currently unreachable fact, which this order forbids presenting as implemented mechanics; or (b) also give the creature a reachable ordinary overrun command with AutoSuccess false, which is new gameplay surface beyond the printed stat block and would need its own qualification; or (c) record the printed feat as present-but-unreachable with this evidence and take no action. No option is taken unilaterally.
GreaterOverrun.disposition: OPEN, with the exact failed path and the smallest choice attached, as the order directs. Not carried, and not waived.
evidence: reflection metadata for ManeuverBonus, ManeuverDefenceBonus, PrerequisiteFeature and PrerequisiteStatValue

printedRulesCorrection.whatWasWrong: This ledger previously stated that the printed Greater Overrun feat removes provocation. That is wrong, and it was the wrong feat: removing the overrunning actor’s own provocation is IMPROVED Overrun.
printedRulesCorrection.improvedOverrunPrinted: The overrunning actor does not provoke an attack of opportunity for performing the maneuver, and it carries its own maneuver bonuses.
printedRulesCorrection.greaterOverrunPrinted: An additional +2 on overrun checks, stacking with Improved Overrun, and opponents knocked prone by the overrun provoke attacks of opportunity.
printedRulesCorrection.scope: These establish the printed rules only. What the installed engine does is recorded separately below, from its own code.
